clue.text: Means to get around town – using quiet donkey

blocks.note: by means of, using
p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A traveller plans to skirt a busy town on a quiet donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road built so traffic can go round a town instead of through it.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature: George Dubya when very young?

blocks.note: George W. ('Dubya') Bush, US president
someone very young is a baby

explanation.surface: A joking picture of a former president as an infant, roaming at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubya' is the nickname for George W. Bush, from a Texan saying of his middle initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby, or galago, is a small big-eyed African primate active at night.

clue.text: Artist detained by dim female lawyer's assistant

indicators.note: someone detained by another is held in custody, so these letters sit inside

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a pale or dim light is faint
a gal is an informal word for a woman

explanation.surface: An artist is held by a dull-witted woman who works for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paralegal is trained in legal matters and assists solicitors without being fully qualified.

clue.text: Composer getting me into Satan – awful!

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it
something awful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer finds himself possessed by the Devil, and it is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the Czech composer of Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Covered pupils before illness gone?

blocks.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school
when an illness has gone the patient is cured

explanation.surface: Pupils were kept covered up until their illness passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' just places the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is hidden from view, as if covered over.

clue.text: A way to make peace? It's no good if you've an axe to grind!

blocks.note: straight reading: an idiom for ending a quarrel

blocks.clueFragment: It's no good if you've an axe to grind
blocks.note: setter's reading: taken literally, a buried axe cannot be sharpened, and having an axe to grind means holding a grudge

explanation.walkthrough: 'An axe to grind' is an idiom for a grudge; literally, you cannot sharpen an axe you have put in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to settle a quarrel and become reconciled, from a Native American peace custom.

clue.text: Military type sounds like a nut!

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to match the spoken form of a word

blocks.note: a kernel is the edible inside of a nut

explanation.surface: A jibe that an army officer is a crackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like slang for a madman; it is the edible kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer, ranking above a lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Bird concerning First Lady

blocks.note: re means concerning, about
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A news item about a bird and a president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' points to a president's spouse, but it means the Biblical first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: Dislike of French experiment

blocks.note: de is French for of
a test is an experiment

explanation.surface: Disapproval of a French scientific trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to hate intensely, a strong form of dislike as a verb.

clue.text: Different classes read old manuscripts

indicators.note: making something different changes its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Various classes study ancient manuscripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks part of the definition but belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea Scrolls are ancient Jewish manuscripts found in caves at Qumran.

clue.text: Positive about golf upswing

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters go round the second

blocks.note: positive means certain, sure
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer feels confident about the upswing in their game.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rise or increase, an upswing in level or activity.

clue.text: Registration of ten men or, confusingly, about fifty?

indicators.note: things presented confusingly are jumbled, so the letters are mixed up
about means around, so the mixed letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A clerk is muddled over whether ten men or about fifty have signed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing up or being entered on a list, which is registration.

clue.text: Poet penning ordinary lines in post

indicators.note: a poet penning something writes it inside, so the poet holds the other letters

blocks.note: a bard is a poet
O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary
L stands for line, so two make lines

explanation.surface: A poet writes a few plain lines and puts them in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests mail, but it is a solid upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollard is a short thick post, used to block traffic or moor boats.

clue.text: Delicate bridge player's bids

blocks.note: tender means delicate, easily hurt
South is one of the four players at bridge, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A cautious bridge player makes gentle bids.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'bids' toward bridge auctions; here it is plain offers of a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenders are formal offers to do work or buy something at a stated price, i.e. bids.

clue.text: Where you can get your own back, having come a long way?

definitions.text: Where you can get your own back, having come a long way?

blocks.note: surface reading: take revenge after a long struggle
setter's reading: the airport hall where travellers collect their luggage after a flight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your own back' sounds like revenge; read literally it is collecting your own suitcases.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport, arriving passengers pick up their checked luggage in this hall after a long journey.

clue.text: Happening right now, I'm given work on a dispute

blocks.note: taken as written
to mediate is to work to settle a dispute

explanation.surface: Someone is told to start resolving a quarrel straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immediate happens at once, with no delay.

clue.text: Huge American going after English standard doughnut

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a norm is a standard
a ring doughnut is O-shaped
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A big American eats after the English standard doughnut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going after' places the American piece at the end, behind the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very large, a synonym of huge.

clue.text: Agitated leaders sent me, with head of tribunal, to find experienced politicians

indicators.note: agitated things are stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
the opening letter of tribunal

explanation.surface: Worried party leaders packed someone off to a tribunal to seek out seasoned politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder statesmen are senior, respected politicians whose long experience gives them influence.

clue.text: Sells abroad from former docklands

blocks.note: ex means former
ports are harbours with docks

explanation.surface: A country ships goods overseas from its old docks.
explanation.definitionFit: To export is to sell goods to another country, so exports is the verb for selling abroad.

clue.text: Sensation resulting from ecstasy and movement

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
motion is movement

explanation.surface: A rush of feeling at a rave from a pill and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling, and sensation can mean a felt response or feeling.

clue.text: Flowers returned in vases, in autumn

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow
returned means sent back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: Flowers given back, standing in vases in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' is not a river here but the plants themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is an umbelliferous plant bearing small white flowers, grown for its aniseed.

clue.text: One with no chance or phone broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so its letters can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck without a working phone has no chance of getting through.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is an informal term for a person with no prospect of success.

clue.text: Large animal cool by river abroad

blocks.note: hip is slang for cool, fashionable
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A big beast cools off beside a foreign river.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippo, short for hippopotamus, is a massive African river mammal.

clue.text: Dog gets the German soup

blocks.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog
der is German for the (masculine)

explanation.surface: A dog is served the German soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, typically made with seafood or corn.

clue.text: Stick with this and you might have difficulty letting go!

definitions.text: Stick with this and you might have difficulty letting go!

blocks.note: surface reading: persevere with a task or habit you will struggle to give up
setter's reading: a very strong adhesive that bonds fingers together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick with' sounds like perseverance; read literally it is gluing things together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast-setting cyanoacrylate adhesive notorious for gluing users' fingers together.

clue.text: State, on the radio: "I owned a garden tool"

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.note: owned is had, and a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: A radio caller from somewhere in America reminisces about a hoe they once owned.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Director makes his mark with first of Emmys, embraces son

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter
to embrace is to hold within your arms, so the other letters wrap round

blocks.note: to score is to make a mark, like a scratch or a tally
the opening letter of Emmys
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A film director leaves his mark by winning Emmys and hugging his son.
explanation.walkthrough: The son sits inside the run of letters from 'makes his mark', just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American film director of Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: Starts parts of a tennis match, after running

indicators.note: after tells us the tennis piece follows the piece for running, not the reverse of the clue's order

blocks.note: a machine or show that is running is on
a tennis match is divided into sets

explanation.surface: A tennis match begins, with sets played after a warm-up run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the tennis piece behind the 'running' piece, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, so onsets are starts.
